key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence can non-destructively distinguish whether degradation in perovskite solar cells starts at the ETL/perovskite interface or spreads into the absorber under heat.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical diagnostic for evaluating passivation strategies like PEABF4 and for tracking depth-resolved stability losses during device aging.
method: Excitation-wavelength-dependent PL mapping to probe different depths nondestructively
Compare fresh vs thermally aged PEABF4-treated and untreated stacks
Use diffusion-recombination simulations to interpret PL decay in terms of surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PEABF4 reduces interfacial recombination initially, but thermal aging causes faster PL decay and a broader loss profile extending from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber.
watch_item: PL-based depth interpretation depends on model assumptions and may be sensitive to sample optics, so calibration is needed before generalizing across device architectures.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
